analysis:
This batch has no executable code. It contains a changelog (changelog.d/nemotron-super-media-discovery.md), a hardware-support.md edit (a Super builder note at lines 13-18 plus a date bump), and the inference.md metadata and a truncated patch.

The changelog documents these new opt-in and unregistered paths:
- The Super owner serves text and images through an HTTP hook that is disabled by default and reuses existing auth, SSE and cancellation. It accepts consumer-controlled PNG and JPEG through a CPU ImageIO decoder with geometry bounds, which is untrusted-media attack surface (see T-050 for the inline-video analogue).
- MTP speculation (env opt-in), a concurrency env (up to 8), and tool_calls and response_format validation.
- A resident prefix checkpoint bank (`DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY=1`, lines 57-63). I flagged this as conflicting with the T-041 'no production RAM tier' statement and with `ramPrefix` being 0 in production.

The hardware-support.md change preserves the load-lease and concurrency-floor policy and weakens no control. The inference.md patch is truncated: only its metadata unit was supplied, so the Super binding, drain and ownership code descriptions were not seen. No source code was supplied, so the claims are unverified: HTTP auth, the salt scoping of the checkpoint bank, the decoder bounds, the 429 busy handling, and whether unregistered means unreachable from the coordinator. Later passes should check the actual implementation files (NemotronSuperLocalBridgeBuilder, the owner hook, and the media decoder) for these.

findings.detail: The changelog adds `DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY=1`, which opts the Nemotron Super owner into exact text prefix reuse through a resident recurrent checkpoint bank. The bank is sized at min(1 GiB, grant/8) and reserved from load until retirement. T-041 and its mitigations say production never constructs or funds a resident-RAM prefix cache and that there is no production RAM tier. docs/architecture/hardware-support.md still says `ramPrefix` is always 0. This is a new cross-request reuse surface: a hit skips prefill, so first-token latency leaks whether another prompt shared the prefix (the T-041 TTFT oracle). Retained checkpoints also leave decoded prompt-derived state resident in process memory after the request completes (T-028). The visible text does not say whether the bank is keyed by the coordinator-authored cacheSalt or whether it is bound to model build and prompt contract. It does say client prompt-cache keys are rejected, but that does not establish tenant isolation. The T-041 sign-off, the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE kill-switch semantics and the TTL bounds do not obviously cover this path. Fix: update T-041 and TB-007 to describe this tier; state its scope key, eviction and TTL bounds, and whether the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 kill switch also disables it; and require salt-scoped lookup before the owner is registered or enabled for multi-tenant traffic.
findings.title: Opt-in resident RAM prefix-checkpoint bank contradicts T-041's 'no production RAM tier' posture
